title: fix(lint): refuse a react-page ListView bound only by the canonical data source
body:
Part of #14791

**Step 1 of 3** of the maintainer's ruling B (recorded on the card, 2026-09-03, verbatim 「同意」). This is the spec lane's step 1 only — the validator stops blessing a react-page ListView bound only by the canonical spelling. The card stays open: step 2 (objectui's consumer fold) and step 3 (retire the aliases, re-enable canonical binding, rename the sites) remain. objectui#7477 is step 2. #14343 remains blocked until step 3.

⛔ No site renames, no `packages/spec` change, nothing in objectui — all three are later steps.

## The defect

The react-blocks contract deprecates ListView's `objectName` in favour of `data={{ provider: 'object', object }}`, and this rule treated a present `deprecated.replacedBy` as satisfying the required binding. No renderer reads that spelling, so a page written to the contract's own summary passed `os validate` and then rendered an empty list with no diagnostic. The rule's own comment justified its canonical-first precedence as "mirroring the one-directional fold objectui's `normalizeListViewSchema` applies at the component boundary" — that fold does not exist.

Re-measured on the objectui tip `a27d153c`, newer than the readings on the card, in `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`:

| spelling | occurrences |
|:--|--:|
| `data.object` | 0 |
| `dataConfig.object` | 0 |
| `provider === 'object'` | 0 |
| `specType` | 0 |
| `schema.objectName` | 52 |

`packages/core/src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts` contains zero `.object` reads. The premise holds.

## What changed — `packages/lint/src/validate-react-page-props.ts`

- The replaced-by satisfaction no longer applies to ListView's object binding when the author wrote the object provider (`objectProviderBindsNothing`, a named exception citing the ruling). The generic mechanism the contract publishes is kept for every other block.
- `boundObjectName` drops its canonical-first branch. Field-name props resolve against `objectName` again — which is also the correct object when a page carries both spellings, since that is the one the renderer queries.
- The false fold comment is gone. What replaces it records, dated, that the fold does not exist, so the assumption cannot be reintroduced by the next reader.
- The missing-required diagnostic no longer offers `data={…} (canonical)` for ListView; it names `objectName`, and adds one clause explaining that the canonical source would render an empty list. The deprecation warning keeps its severity and now says `objectName` / `viewType` are still the spellings to write.

## One measured refinement to the dispatch

The dispatch framed the tightening as ListView losing the replaced-by satisfaction. Measurement narrowed it to the **object provider only**. `ListView.tsx`'s fetch effect implements `provider: 'value'`, a plain-array shorthand and the renderer-owned `api` provider; only `provider: 'object'` falls through all three to the `objectName`-gated fetch, which clears the loading state and returns no rows. Refusing the providers that do render would tighten past what renders, against this step's own stated reason (`Clause-②: no`). A non-static `data` still satisfies — unresolvable is not wrong, ADR-0072 D1. All three cases are pinned.

Blast radius measured, not assumed: ListView is the **only** block in `react-blocks.ts` declaring any `deprecated` prop, so a ListView-scoped exception and a general change are behaviourally identical today. The scoped one was chosen because deleting the mechanism outright would falsify the contract's own doc comment in `packages/spec`, which step 3 owns and this PR may not touch.

## Tests

The vocabulary-window cases that pinned the canonical spelling as binding are **inverted, not deleted** — the window is still open, only its blessing is withdrawn. Two new pins: a canonical-only page is refused with a diagnostic naming `objectName`; an `objectName` page passes. Three more pin the scope (value provider, non-static `data`, and the deprecated spelling winning when both are present).

Every other ListView fixture merely used the canonical spelling as a convenient binding; each is re-spelled to `objectName`, without which those suites would resolve fields against nothing and pass vacuously. That adds one deprecation warning per fixture, so the field-resolution suites read past that single rule.

**No real site goes red.** All five checked-in ListView sites bind with `objectName`: `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md:180` and `:218`, `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/crm-workbench.page.ts:88`, `renewals-pipeline.page.ts:136` and `:169`, `task-desk.page.ts:44`. Zero sites anywhere write the canonical spelling. The other `provider: 'object'` hits in the repo are metadata-tier list views, a different schema this rule never reads.

## Verification — all at the final commit `3120681a`

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` — 93 files, 2873 passed, 5 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` — clean, including the shrink-only test-layer ratchet (`check:test-typecheck: OK`).
- Gate family re-derived on the actual diff with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` after the merge, from a tree with no staleness warning: **36 of 39 pass**. The other three exit **3**, their own "PREREQUISITE NOT MET" code, which each states is neither a pass nor a finding: `check-test-completeness` needs a saved turbo test log CI tees and this branch cannot produce, and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` / `check:type-check-debt` need every package's `dist`. Recorded as NOT MEASURED; CI measures them.
- **Reverse verification**, fix committed first, direction predicted before running: restoring only the source to the pre-fix base should turn the new pins red. Mutation confirmed on disk by marker counts (guard 3 to 0, removed comment 0 to 1) and a blob hash differing from HEAD; result **6 failed / 157 passed**, exactly the six predicted cases, the 22 re-spelled fixtures staying green as predicted. Restore proven by observed state, not an exit code: `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status --porcelain` empty (no poisoned index), and the file byte-identical to the HEAD blob `e94f2370`. No build leg is involved — the suite imports the rule by relative path, so vitest reads the mutated source directly.
- **Declared narrowing:** the repo-wide `pnpm lint` was not run; `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` ran on the two changed files, 0 errors and 0 warnings, file count 2 read from the JSON output. This cannot have moved any untouched file's verdict: `eslint.config.mjs:327-329` states this repo "never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules) for ANY file".
